note: Verses as the study API publishes them. Do not hand-edit "text": run `python tools/test_readings.py --refresh`. An earlier version of these cases was typed by hand, and a truncated 2 Nephi 2:7 passed a test the published verse fails.

cases.why: Reaches 'God' only after three pronouns. The verse reported as broken.
cases.text: And they rehearsed unto his father all that had happened unto them; and his father rejoiced, for he knew that it was the power of God.

cases.why: 'And said,' -- the speaker is back in verse 20. Reported as broken.
cases.text: And said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.

cases.why: 'he offereth himself' wants Christ named; 2 Nephi 2:6 names him, 2:7 does not. Its closing 'unto none else' is who the verse is for, not who it is about.
cases.text: Behold, he offereth himself a sacrifice for sin, to answer the ends of the law, unto all those who have a broken heart and a contrite spirit; and unto none else can the ends of the law be answered.

cases.why: The pronoun is the only subject there is, so the reader has to bring one.
cases.text: And again, behold I say unto you that he cannot have faith and hope, save he shall be meek, and lowly of heart.

cases.why: 'this much' is a fronted object; the subject is 'I' and the address is 'you'.
cases.text: But this much I can tell you, that if ye do not watch yourselves, and your thoughts, and your words, and your deeds, and observe the commandments of God, and continue in the faith of what ye have heard concerning the coming of our Lord, even unto the end of your lives, ye must perish. And now, O man, remember, and perish not.

cases.why: 'this is not all' is a turn in the argument; the teaching lands after it.
cases.text: But this is not all; they had given themselves to much prayer, and fasting; therefore they had the spirit of prophecy, and the spirit of revelation, and when they taught, they taught with power and authority of God.

cases.why: Plural reads as generic: a reader supplies 'people who do this'.
cases.text: Nevertheless they did fast and pray oft, and did wax stronger and stronger in their humility, and firmer and firmer in the faith of Christ, unto the filling their souls with joy and consolation, yea, even to the purifying and the sanctification of their hearts, which sanctification cometh because of their yielding their hearts unto God.

cases.why: Restates its teaching with a subject in it -- 'none is acceptable', 'if a man be meek'.
cases.text: If so, his faith and hope is vain, for none is acceptable before God, save the meek and lowly in heart; and if a man be meek and lowly in heart, and confesses by the power of the Holy Ghost that Jesus is the Christ, he must needs have charity; for if he have not charity he is nothing; wherefore he must needs have charity.

cases.why: Plural opener, and the verse names the Spirit of the Lord Omnipotent itself.
cases.text: And they all cried with one voice, saying: Yea, we believe all the words which thou hast spoken unto us; and also, we know of their surety and truth, because of the Spirit of the Lord Omnipotent, which has wrought a mighty change in us, or in our hearts, that we have no more disposition to do evil, but to do good continually.

cases.why: 'While he was yet speaking' -- a messenger's report to a man never named.
cases.text: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep, and the servants, and consumed them; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

cases.why: 'And behold, he preached' -- nothing at all in front of the pronoun.
cases.text: And behold, he preached the word unto your fathers, and a mighty change was also wrought in their hearts, and they humbled themselves and put their trust in the true and living God. And behold, they were faithful until the end; therefore they were saved.

cases.why: 'And he had hope to shake me from the faith' is Sherem, and reads like counsel.
cases.text: And he had hope to shake me from the faith, notwithstanding the many revelations and the many things which I had seen concerning these things; for I truly had seen angels, and they had ministered unto me. And also, I had heard the voice of the Lord speaking unto me in very word, from time to time; wherefore, I could not be shaken.

cases.why: 'And he commanded them' -- narrative with the speaker offstage.
cases.text: And he commanded them that they should observe the sabbath day, and keep it holy, and also every day they should give thanks to the Lord their God.

cases.why: 'And he commandeth all men' -- 'all men' is the object, not an antecedent.
cases.text: And he commandeth all men that they must repent, and be baptized in his name, having perfect faith in the Holy One of Israel, or they cannot be saved in the kingdom of God.

cases.why: 'these are those who' -- a demonstrative handing off to another pronoun.
cases.text: And these are those who have part in the first resurrection; and these are they that have died before Christ came, in their ignorance, not having salvation declared unto them. And thus the Lord bringeth about the restoration of these; and they have a part in the first resurrection, or have eternal life, being redeemed by the Lord.

cases.why: 'And this was done' -- a demonstrative handing off to an undescribed act.
cases.text: Now this was done in the presence of the queen and many of the servants. And when they saw it they greatly marveled, and began to fear. And the king stood forth, and began to minister unto them. And he did minister unto them, insomuch that his whole household were converted unto the Lord.

cases.why: Narrative; 'him' and 'he' are never answered.
cases.text: And it came to pass that they were angry with him, even because he had greater power than they, for it were not possible that they could disbelieve his words, for so great was his faith on the Lord Jesus Christ that angels did minister unto him daily.

cases.why: 'And he shall come' with nothing before it; 'none else' carries no verb.
cases.text: And he shall come into the world to redeem his people; and he shall take upon him the transgressions of those who believe on his name; and these are they that shall have eternal life, and salvation cometh to none else.

cases.why: 'He doeth not anything' opens the verse; 'commandeth none that' is not a subject.
cases.text: He doeth not anything save it be for the benefit of the world; for he loveth the world, even that he layeth down his own life that he may draw all men unto him. Wherefore, he commandeth none that they shall not partake of his salvation.

cases.why: 'he was a man who was firm' is Moroni, and 'a man who' heads no clause.
cases.text: Yea, and he was a man who was firm in the faith of Christ, and he had sworn with an oath to defend his people, his rights, and his country, and his religion, even to the loss of his blood.

cases.why: Arrives at a conviction of its own: 'yet will I trust in him'.
cases.text: Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him: but I will maintain mine own ways before him.

cases.why: Same: 'For I know that my redeemer liveth'.
cases.text: For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth:

cases.why: The generic 'He that' means whoever fits and needs nobody named.
cases.text: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

cases.why: Plural generic, 'they that wait upon the Lord'.
cases.text: But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.

cases.why: 'seeketh not her own' rests on 'charity', a gospel word the verse opened with.
cases.text: And charity suffereth long, and is kind, and envieth not, and is not puffed up, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil, and rejoiceth not in iniquity but rejoiceth in the truth, beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.

cases.why: 'unto a man, if he shall pray' -- a generic antecedent stands before the pronoun.
cases.text: And likewise also is it counted evil unto a man, if he shall pray and not with real intent of heart; yea, and it profiteth him nothing, for God receiveth none such.

cases.why: 'for a man sometimes, if he is compelled to be humble'.
cases.text: And now, because ye are compelled to be humble blessed are ye; for a man sometimes, if he is compelled to be humble, seeketh repentance; and now surely, whosoever repenteth shall find mercy; and he that findeth mercy and endureth to the end the same shall be saved.

cases.why: 'trust no one to be your teacher ... except he be a man of God'.
cases.text: And also trust no one to be your teacher nor your minister, except he be a man of God, walking in his ways and keeping his commandments.

cases.why: 'this is not all' left alone; the teaching lands immediately after.
cases.text: But this is not all; ye must pour out your souls in your closets, and your secret places, and in your wilderness.

cases.why: Names God and the Lord before it says 'his'.
cases.text: And they were called the people of God. And the Lord did pour out his Spirit upon them, and they were blessed, and prospered in the land.

cases.why: 'thus said Jesus Christ' -- an attribution that names its speaker.
cases.text: For behold, thus said Jesus Christ, the Son of God, unto his disciples who should tarry, yea, and also to all his disciples, in the hearing of the multitude: Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature;

cases.why: 'this is my doctrine' names the thing it means.
cases.text: And this is my doctrine, and it is the doctrine which the Father hath given unto me; and I bear record of the Father, and the Father beareth record of me, and the Holy Ghost beareth record of the Father and me; and I bear record that the Father commandeth all men, everywhere, to repent and believe in me.

cases.why: 'this is life eternal' likewise.
cases.text: And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.

cases.why: The expletive 'It is better ...' stands in for nothing at all.
cases.text: Behold the Lord slayeth the wicked to bring forth his righteous purposes. It is better that one man should perish than that a nation should dwindle and perish in unbelief.

cases.why: Plural, and addressed in the first and second person throughout.
cases.text: And if men come unto me I will show unto them their weakness. I give unto men weakness that they may be humble; and my grace is sufficient for all men that humble themselves before me; for if they humble themselves before me, and have faith in me, then will I make weak things become strong unto them.

cases.why: Names Adam; no third-person singular pronoun to answer.
cases.text: Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.

cases.why: 'it is mockery' is the baptising of little children, back in 8:22. Reported as broken: the verse calls something a mockery and never says what.
cases.text: But it is mockery before God, denying the mercies of Christ, and the power of his Holy Spirit, and putting trust in dead works.

cases.why: 'They are raised' -- who is raised is the whole question, and 15:24 is where it is answered. Reported as broken.
cases.text: They are raised to dwell with God who has redeemed them; thus they have eternal life through Christ, who has broken the bands of death.

cases.why: 'It is because you have hardened your hearts' answers a question asked in 7:17.
cases.text: It is because you have hardened your hearts; yea, ye will not hearken unto the voice of the good shepherd; yea, ye have provoked him to anger against you.

cases.why: 'they were married, and given in marriage, and were blessed' -- done to them, never by them, and nobody named.
cases.text: And they were married, and given in marriage, and were blessed according to the multitude of the promises which the Lord had made unto them.

cases.why: 'And also that we may preserve' -- a stacked conjunction in front of the fragment, and what is preserved for is back in 3:19. Ruled a close call rather than a clear one: a reader who knows the chapter takes 'them' as everyone after Lehi and loses nothing. It is refused because the site is read by people who do not have 3:19 in front of them; if it were ever only for its author, this case is the one to revisit.
cases.text: And also that we may preserve unto them the words which have been spoken by the mouth of all the holy prophets, which have been delivered unto them by the Spirit and power of God, since the world began, even down unto this present time.

cases.why: 'And also that nation, whom they shall serve' -- which nation, and whose seed serves it, are both back in 15:13. Ruled on after the pattern refused it: the reading is right even though 'that' is a determiner here.
cases.text: And also that nation, whom they shall serve, will I judge: and afterward shall they come out with great substance.

cases.why: 'And again, that same God has brought our fathers out' -- 'that' is a determiner here, and the verse is a whole sentence. Ruled a good reading alone: 'that same God' resolves on sight and wants nothing from 7:19.
cases.text: And again, that same God has brought our fathers out of the land of Jerusalem, and has kept and preserved his people even until now; and behold, it is because of our iniquities and abominations that he has brought us into bondage.

cases.why: 'they were men of truth and soberness' names who they are; 'men' is a noun, not the participle it is spelled like.
cases.text: Yea, they were men of truth and soberness, for they had been taught to keep the commandments of God and to walk uprightly before him.

cases.why: The placeholder 'it' is filled by the infinitive after it: 'It is better to trust in the Lord'.
cases.text: It is better to trust in the Lord than to put confidence in man.

cases.why: Same shape: 'It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God'.
cases.text: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

cases.why: 'it shall come to pass' carries what follows without a complementiser to mark it.
cases.text: And it shall come to pass in the last days, saith God, I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams:

cases.why: 'it is written' -- the 'it' is the quotation after the comma.
cases.text: For it is written, As I live, saith the Lord, every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall confess to God.

cases.why: 'this life is the time' -- a demonstrative used as a determiner.
cases.text: For behold, this life is the time for men to prepare to meet God; yea, behold the day of this life is the day for men to perform their labors.
